text:
Recent work separates factual grounding from preference alignment: an explanation can describe an item correctly yet give unsupported reasons why this user wants it. PURE (2026) selects evidence for both factual support and preference consistency ([paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03080)). For these diagnostics, attach each claim to a history event or explicit title/description attribute. Treat missing prerequisites, ownership, compatibility, dislikes, and recently satisfied needs as unknown unless supported; semantic similarity alone cannot establish them.

Complementary and substitute relationships require different evidence: complements support another item’s function; substitutes serve a similar purpose ([function-based complementary recommendation](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0167865525003976)). Temporal work distinguishes recurring intent, long-term interests, and short-term adaptation ([HyperHawkes, 2025](https://evazangerle.at/publication/peintner-www-2025/)); timestamps therefore inform hypotheses about current relevance but do not establish that a need has been satisfied. Specific content matches should identify the shared attribute and its observed historical basis, with prerequisite-dependent usefulness stated conditionally.

Abstention research supports measuring error among accepted predictions alongside coverage; conformal abstention offers error-control guarantees under its calibration assumptions ([2024 paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.01563)). Proposed adaptation—not an established finding for these twenty users: record immediate choice, conditional usefulness, explicit mismatch, and unassessable feedback separately, preserving each denominator and evidence source. Report counts and uncertainty; twenty users cannot support precise category-specific calibration. Conditional usefulness is not immediate-choice success, and missing evidence is not negative preference. Use feedback for diagnostic hypotheses while retaining macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion.
